_about: Profit playbooks: specific ways each industry turns Ledgerlight signals into money, with an end-to-end guide. Shown in the portal (Playbooks tab), linked from the terminal, and featured on all nine websites. Information, not advice: each play lists its guardrails.

plays.title: Protect retentions and unpaid valuations
plays.profit: Stop losing money to failing clients: get paid, or stop supplying, before a main contractor goes under.
plays.money: Illustration: a subcontractor holding £60k of retention across four main contractors that cuts its exposure to the one that fails keeps money that would otherwise rank as an unsecured claim.
steps: Add every client and main contractor to your Watchlist, with the amount owed and the retention you hold on each.
Turn on instant alerts for petitions, administrations, CCJs and new charges on those companies.
When Company Insight moves a client to Elevated or higher, follow its protocol: shorter terms, payment before the next delivery, and a second sign-off for any new order.
Chase every undisputed sum while the warning signs are early. Once a winding-up petition is presented, payments the company makes can be clawed back, so take advice before accepting them.
If the client enters administration or liquidation, lodge your claim with the insolvency practitioner before the claim deadline shown in the alert, and stop supplying on credit.
Open the terminal, press "What this means for you" and choose Customers to see the knock-on risk to your other jobs. Record the decision and, later, the outcome in the decision log.
plays.track: Money owed to companies that later failed, compared with the last 12 months.
plays.guardrails: Information, not legal advice. Take advice on retention claims, set-off and payments received after a petition.

plays.title: Win the work a failed contractor leaves behind
plays.profit: When a contractor fails, its clients still need their sites finished. Be the first credible firm to offer.
plays.money: Illustration: one completion package on a stalled site can be worth more than a year of small tenders, and the client is motivated to move quickly.
steps: Set your feed filters to your trades (SIC codes) and the regions you can cover.
When a contractor fails, open the alert to see its known live sites and public contracts, and export them to CSV.
Check each client in Company Insight first: only chase work from clients that are Low or Watch risk.
Contact the client, and the administrator, who may want contractors to complete works, with a short completion proposal and a start date.
Price in the extra risk: a mobilisation payment, fortnightly valuations, and a project bank account where the client will agree.
Push the leads to your CRM with CRM sync and track which ones convert.
plays.track: Completion contracts won from failure alerts, and their margin.
plays.guardrails: Approach businesses, not individuals. Don't use the failed firm's confidential information.

plays.title: Buy plant, materials and customers from insolvency sales
plays.profit: Plant hire firms, merchants and contractors can buy equipment and stock below market value, and offer accounts to the failed firm's customers.
plays.money: Illustration: plant bought at an insolvency auction and re-hired at your normal rate can pay back far faster than new kit.
steps: Filter alerts to plant hire, builders' merchants and the trades whose equipment you use.
When one fails, call the insolvency practitioner or their appointed agent (both in the alert) to register interest in the assets.
Inspect and bid. The terminal's Opportunity view shows other failures in the same sector, which can depress prices.
Offer trade accounts to the failed firm's customers, but check each one in Company Insight before you give credit.
Record what you bought, the price, and the rental income it earns.
plays.track: Asset cost against new price, and payback period.
plays.guardrails: Buy through the insolvency practitioner's sale process. Check title and finance on every asset.

plays.title: Help displaced sponsored workers find a new sponsor
plays.profit: When a licensed sponsor fails, its sponsored workers usually have a short window to find a new sponsor. Employers with vacancies need help sponsoring them quickly.
plays.money: Illustration: a fixed-fee sponsorship package for each employer that takes on transferring workers, charged to the employer.
steps: Set alerts for sponsors in insolvency or removed from the register, in your regions and sectors (care, hospitality, engineering).
Open the alert to see the sponsor's route and an estimate of how many workers are affected.
Use extraction to list nearby licensed sponsors in the same sector, and check each in Company Insight so you only refer workers to stable employers.
Offer those employers a fixed-fee package: assigning Certificates of Sponsorship, right-to-work checks and record keeping.
Work to the deadline: leave is usually cut to about 60 days, so start the same week.
Log each placement and outcome in your CRM.
plays.track: Employers helped and workers successfully transferred.
plays.guardrails: Charge the employer, not the worker. Sponsors can't recover the Immigration Skills Charge or the Certificate of Sponsorship fee from workers. Only regulated advisers may give immigration advice.

plays.title: Compliance audits for new and changing sponsors
plays.profit: Newly licensed sponsors and companies changing hands have reporting duties they often miss. Sell them an audit before the Home Office does one.
plays.money: Illustration: a fixed-fee mock audit, then a monthly retainer for HR compliance.
steps: Get a weekly digest of newly licensed sponsors in your area.
Add an alert for change of ownership and director changes on licensed sponsors: these can trigger reporting duties to the Home Office.
Export the lists with contact fields and push them to your CRM.
Offer a mock compliance audit with a written report and an action plan.
Turn audits into retainers for ongoing reporting and record keeping.
plays.track: Audits sold, and audits that became retainers.
plays.guardrails: Business contacts only. Check the latest sponsor guidance for deadlines before you advise.

plays.title: Protect placements with sponsoring clients
plays.profit: Recruiters placing sponsored workers lose fees, and workers lose jobs, when a client sponsor fails. Watch clients and switch early.
plays.money: Illustration: keeping one placement fee that would otherwise be refunded under a rebate clause.
steps: Add every client that sponsors your candidates to the Watchlist.
When a client moves to Elevated, pause new placements with it and prepare alternative sponsoring employers.
Use the terminal's Customers view to see sector news that may hit your clients, such as care funding changes.
Record the decision so your team follows the same rule next time.
plays.track: Placements lost to client failures.
plays.guardrails: Treat candidates fairly and keep them informed. Never charge candidates fees.

plays.title: Offer services to the firms handling estates
plays.profit: Many estates are run by solicitors or professional executors who need valuations, property sales, clearance and auctions. Sell to the firm, never to the family.
plays.money: Illustration: one solicitor firm can refer several estates a year once you are its trusted provider.
steps: Complete EstateSignal vetting and accept the code of conduct.
Set your districts and services. Alerts arrive only after the cooling-off period, with the area and the professional firm, never the family's names or address.
Group notices by firm in your extraction: firms that appear often are your best partners.
Approach each firm with a business offer: valuation, sale, clearance or auction, with clear fees.
Track referrals by firm in your CRM.
plays.track: Referral firms signed, and instructions from each.
plays.guardrails: Never contact the family from a notice. Respect the cooling-off period and the code of conduct.

plays.title: Trace heirs to unclaimed estates
plays.profit: Estates with no known heirs are listed publicly. Probate genealogists research the family tree and work for an agreed share of the inheritance.
plays.money: Illustration: an agreed percentage of an estate, paid only if heirs are found and the claim succeeds.
steps: Turn on alerts for newly listed unclaimed estates in your areas of research.
Prioritise by date added and estate size where it is known: newer listings face less competition.
Research the family tree from public records.
Offer any heirs you find a written agreement with clear fees and a cooling-off period.
Make the claim, and record the outcome to sharpen your prioritisation.
plays.track: Cases researched, heirs found, claims paid.
plays.guardrails: Be transparent about fees, and give heirs time to decide. Follow your professional body's code.

plays.title: Buy land owned by dissolved companies
plays.profit: When a company is dissolved its property can pass to the Crown. Investors can buy it from the Crown, or help former directors restore the company and sell.
plays.money: Illustration: buying at a negotiated price from a motivated seller that has no use for the property.
steps: Set alerts for dissolved companies that still hold land titles in your target areas.
Check the title and its history in the alert, and value the property.
Either approach the Crown's bona vacantia office to make an offer, or contact the former directors in their business role about restoring the company and selling.
Take legal advice on restoration and title before you complete.
plays.track: Titles reviewed, offers made, completions.
plays.guardrails: Company and property data only. Take legal advice on every purchase.

plays.title: Reach companies early, while rescue is still possible
plays.profit: Directors who get advice early have more options: refinancing, a CVA, or a sale. Advisers who reach them first win the work.
plays.money: Illustration: a turnaround or CVA engagement started months before a creditor would otherwise force a liquidation.
steps: Set filters for the company size, sectors and regions you serve.
Each morning, review companies whose Company Insight band rose to Elevated or High. The reasons show why.
Check the timeline and connected companies: directors with past insolvencies change the approach.
Use the terminal's Opportunity view to see sector pressure, for example a run of hospitality failures.
Approach directors with a clear, honest offer of an initial review, and transparent fees.
Record each approach and its outcome, so you learn which signals lead to engagements.
plays.track: Approaches, initial meetings, engagements, fees.
plays.guardrails: Follow the Insolvency Code of Ethics: no misleading or high-pressure marketing. Information, not advice.

plays.title: Buy distressed businesses and assets
plays.profit: Administrations and liquidations put businesses, brands, stock and equipment up for sale quickly. Buyers who register interest early get first look.
plays.money: Illustration: buying a business and its assets from an administrator at a discount to going-concern value.
steps: Define your buy box: sector, size, region and price range.
Set alerts on administrations and liquidations that match, with the practitioner's contact details.
Contact the practitioner the same day to register interest and sign a non-disclosure agreement.
Use the Company Insight timeline to understand what went wrong before you bid.
Bid through the practitioner's sale process, and add the business to your Watchlist after completion.
plays.track: Opportunities seen, bids, acquisitions, return on capital.
plays.guardrails: Connected-party pre-pack sales have extra rules, including an independent evaluator's report.

plays.title: Lend to stressed but viable companies
plays.profit: Asset-based lenders can fund companies that banks turn away, if they can tell a cash squeeze from a failing business.
plays.money: Illustration: a secured facility at a premium rate, to a business whose assets cover the loan.
steps: Filter for companies at Watch or Elevated risk that still show positive net assets.
Read the reasons: late filing alone is different from CCJs plus director exits.
Offer a secured facility, and price it to the risk band.
Once lent, add the borrower to your Watchlist and set the two-person rule for any increase.
plays.track: Facilities written, and losses against the risk band at lending.
plays.guardrails: Lending is regulated in some cases. Information, not credit advice.

plays.title: Cut rent losses from failing tenants
plays.profit: Spot a tenant in trouble months early, and secure deposits, guarantees or a planned exit before the arrears build up.
plays.money: Illustration: a rent deposit taken at renewal from a tenant that later failed covers several months' rent.
steps: Add every commercial tenant to the Watchlist, with the rent and the unit.
At each renewal or assignment, check Company Insight: ask for a deposit or a guarantee from Elevated and High tenants.
On a petition or CCJ, contact the tenant early to agree a payment plan, or plan for vacancy.
If the tenant enters administration, remember the moratorium: you need the administrator's consent or the court's permission to forfeit. Lodge your claim.
Use the terminal's Customers view to watch sector news that hits your tenants, such as retail or hospitality failures.
plays.track: Rent arrears written off, compared with last year.
plays.guardrails: Information, not legal advice. Take advice before forfeiture.

plays.title: Re-let empty units quickly
plays.profit: When a chain fails, its competitors and growing local firms want space. Market vacant units to them first.
plays.money: Illustration: cutting a void period by two months on a single unit.
steps: When a retailer or restaurant chain fails, export the list of its sites in your area.
Find competitors and growing firms in the same sector with extraction filters (sector, region, recent growth).
Check each prospect tenant in Company Insight before you agree heads of terms.
Send them a short list of available units, and track enquiries in your CRM.
plays.track: Void months saved, and lettings from these leads.
plays.guardrails: Business contacts only.

plays.title: Buy property from insolvent and dissolved owners
plays.profit: Property-owning companies in administration need to sell, and dissolved companies can leave land behind.
plays.money: Illustration: buying from an administrator who needs a quick sale.
steps: Set alerts on property-owning companies entering administration or being dissolved, in your target areas.
Review the titles in the alert and value them.
Contact the administrator or the Crown's bona vacantia office to make an offer.
Take legal advice on title before you complete.
plays.track: Titles reviewed, offers, completions.
plays.guardrails: Take legal advice on every purchase.

plays.title: Place skilled staff released by an insolvency
plays.profit: When an employer fails, whole teams look for work overnight. Recruiters who move first place them with clients who need those skills.
plays.money: Illustration: several placements from one administration, at your normal fee.
steps: Set alerts for administrations and liquidations of employers in your sectors and within your radius.
Open the alert to see the headcount and likely roles.
Within 48 hours, post the matching vacancies you hold, targeted at that area and skill set.
Offer the administrator help running a jobs day for the affected staff.
Tell hiring clients that experienced people are available, using the terminal to explain the news.
Track candidates and placements in your CRM.
plays.track: Placements from each insolvency alert.
plays.guardrails: Don't scrape personal data. Reach candidates through adverts and channels they choose.

plays.title: Sell outplacement to administrators and buyers
plays.profit: Administrators and the buyers of failed businesses often need redundancy support and outplacement.
plays.money: Illustration: a fixed-fee outplacement programme for a site closure.
steps: Set alerts for administrations with large headcounts.
Contact the practitioner with a fixed-fee outplacement offer.
When the business is sold, offer the buyer help restructuring the team.
Record wins and repeat with the same practitioner firms.
plays.track: Programmes sold, and repeat practitioner firms.
plays.guardrails: Business contacts only.

plays.title: Win hiring clients among growing companies
plays.profit: Companies that just raised money, won public contracts or crossed size thresholds are about to hire.
plays.money: Illustration: a new client that hires several people in its first year.
steps: Filter for companies with new funding, contract wins or growth in your sectors.
Use the terminal to read the deal and funding news behind them.
Check Company Insight: avoid clients at Elevated risk, whose fees may never be paid.
Approach the hiring manager with a short, relevant shortlist.
plays.track: New clients won, and fees billed.
plays.guardrails: Business contacts only.

plays.title: Set credit limits from live risk
plays.profit: Fewer bad debts and faster cash, by matching each customer's terms to its current risk.
plays.money: Illustration: cutting bad debt by a fraction of a percent of turnover is often worth more than a price rise.
steps: Upload your ledger to the Watchlist, with the amount owed by each customer.
Agree a policy by band: Low normal terms; Watch review; Elevated lower limit and shorter terms; High payment up front and a second sign-off; Critical stop credit and claim.
Let alerts trigger the policy automatically, and review the watchlist ranked by risk every week.
Use the decision log so every limit change has a reason and a second reviewer where the rule needs one.
Compare outcomes against bands each quarter, and tighten or relax the policy.
plays.track: Bad debt as a share of sales, and days sales outstanding.
plays.guardrails: Information, not credit advice.

plays.title: Collect from the riskiest customers first
plays.profit: Work the ledger in order of risk times amount, so the cash at most risk comes in first.
plays.money: Illustration: collecting an overdue invoice a month before the customer's petition is presented.
steps: Sort your watchlist by risk band, then amount owed.
Call the top of the list first and agree dates for every overdue amount.
For High-risk customers, stop further supply until overdue amounts are paid.
If a petition appears, take advice before accepting payments, because they can be clawed back.
plays.track: Cash collected from High and Critical customers before they failed.
plays.guardrails: Collect fairly and lawfully.

plays.title: Grow sales with your safest customers
plays.profit: Raise limits for Low-risk and improving customers to win share that cautious competitors leave behind.
plays.money: Illustration: extra orders from customers your competitors have put on stop.
steps: Filter your watchlist for Low-risk customers with a falling or stable trend.
Offer them higher limits or better terms in exchange for more volume.
Use the terminal's sector view to spot sectors where competitors are likely to tighten credit.
Review these customers monthly and act at once if the band rises.
plays.track: Extra sales to Low-risk customers, and bad debt on them.
plays.guardrails: Information, not credit advice.

plays.title: Win new companies in their first weeks
plays.profit: New companies need an accountant, a bank, insurance and a website. The first helpful offer usually wins.
plays.money: Illustration: a first-year package for new companies that becomes an annual client.
steps: Get a daily or weekly digest of new companies in your area and the sectors you know.
Export them with registered office and sector, and push them to your CRM.
Send a short welcome letter: first deadlines, a first-year package and a free first meeting.
Follow up before the first confirmation statement is due.
plays.track: New-company clients won per month.
plays.guardrails: New limited companies are corporate subscribers; check the rules before emailing sole traders or partnerships.

plays.title: Rescue companies with overdue accounts
plays.profit: Companies with overdue accounts face penalties that rise the longer they wait, and a risk of being struck off. Many need a new accountant.
plays.money: Illustration: a catch-up filing fee, then an ongoing compliance package.
steps: Set alerts for companies in your area whose accounts or confirmation statements are overdue.
Prioritise those near a strike-off proposal: they need help most urgently.
Check Company Insight: overdue accounts plus CCJs means the company may struggle to pay you, so ask for fees up front.
Offer a fixed-fee catch-up service, then a yearly package.
plays.track: Catch-up jobs won, and how many become annual clients.
plays.guardrails: Business contacts only. Be accurate about penalties.

plays.title: Advise companies as they grow
plays.profit: Companies approaching the VAT threshold or moving to larger accounts need advice and better systems.
plays.money: Illustration: a VAT registration and bookkeeping upgrade for a fast-growing client.
steps: Filter for companies whose filed accounts show turnover approaching the VAT threshold or a jump in size.
Use the terminal to read sector news that explains the growth.
Offer a growth review: VAT, payroll, systems and funding.
Track which signals lead to engagements.
plays.track: Growth reviews sold.
plays.guardrails: Information, not tax advice.
